title: CB-230 keep-or-stop

summary:
The meeting focused on the strategic viability of CB-230 in light of the company's post-GSK financial position. Priya Raman argued for the preservation of the program, asserting that the neuroinflammation biologic represents a core pillar of the company's scientific identity and long-term discovery potential. She emphasized that abandoning CB-230 now would signal a retreat from the high-risk, high-reward research that defines Continental Bio.

Marcus Hale pushed back, centering the discussion on capital allocation and the 2027 portfolio decision. He argued that while the GSK windfall has provided a temporary cushion, the company must prioritize the clinical progression of CB-201 and the upcoming pre-IND milestones for CB-214. Marcus insisted that a definitive decision to either fund CB-230 or seek a partner/exit must be made before the year-end to ensure a clean budget and strategy presentation for the January board meeting.

The debate remained unresolved regarding the specific criteria for a "kill-or-partner" decision. While there was a consensus that the current discovery-stage status of CB-230 cannot continue indefinitely without a clear roadmap, the group could not agree on whether the program should be prioritized for internal development or aggressively shopped to external partners to preserve cash. The tension between maintaining a discovery platform and narrowing the focus to clinical assets remains the central friction point.

Decisions
CB-230 will remain active through the current fiscal year, but will be subject to a formal strategic review before the January board meeting.
